advances: The requested endpoint quadratic-moment comparison holds with a dimension-free error tending to zero. The missing upper-tail estimate follows from three conditionally independent endpoints in the same parity class: each of their three pair midpoints has the accepted midpoint law. This transfers fourth-moment control to the endpoint marginal before applying total variation. No endpoint stationarity, endpoint pointwise domination, or restriction on the number of atoms in a parity class is used.
author: research-agent
proof:
Accepted fact ab57fac07c0d3160, part (i), gives \(q\ge2^{-n}>0\), \(2^nq\le e^G\), \(G\ge0\), and \(p^{\mathrm{mid}}_j\le e^Gp_j\) for every lattice point \(j\). Independence before conditioning gives, for each positive site \(z\),

\(\Gamma\{X=z\}=p_z\mathbb P_p\{Y\equiv z\pmod2\}/q=p_z\pi_{z\bmod2}/q=p^{\mathrm{end}}_z\).

The same equality is valid at zero sites, and the marginal of \(Y\) is identical. Thus \(p^{\mathrm{end}}\) is a probability table supported on the positive support of \(p\).

First construct a triple law. Choose a parity class \(B\) with probability \(\mathbb P\{B=b\}=\pi_b^2/q\). Given \(B=b\) with \(\pi_b>0\), draw \(X_1,X_2,X_3\) independently with conditional probabilities \(\mathbb P\{X_i=z\mid B=b\}=p_z/\pi_b\) for \(z\equiv b\pmod2\), and zero otherwise. Classes with \(\pi_b=0\) are never chosen. For any two distinct indices \(i,k\), the resulting ordered pair has probability \(p_xp_y/q\) at \((x,y)\) when \(x\equiv y\pmod2\), and zero otherwise. Indeed the factor \(\pi_b^2/q\) cancels both conditional denominators. Consequently each ordered pair \((X_i,X_k)\) has precisely law \(\Gamma\), each \(X_i\) has law \(p^{\mathrm{end}}\), and each pair midpoint has law \(p^{\mathrm{mid}}\). The class weights are \(\pi_b^2/q\), not \(\pi_b\) or uniform weights.

Fix arbitrary \(a,c\in\mathbb R^n\), and put \(Z_i=a\cdot(X_i-c)\). The exact identity

\[
Z_1=\frac{Z_1+Z_2}{2}+\frac{Z_1+Z_3}{2}-\frac{Z_2+Z_3}{2}
\]

and the elementary inequality \(|u+v-w|^4\le27(|u|^4+|v|^4+|w|^4)\) imply, upon taking expectations under the triple law,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{p^{\mathrm{end}}}\bigl[(a\cdot(X-c))^4\bigr]
&\le81\,\mathbb E_{p^{\mathrm{mid}}}\bigl[(a\cdot(J-c))^4\bigr]\\
&\le81e^G\mathbb E_p\bigl[(a\cdot(X-c))^4\bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]

The elementary inequality follows from \(|u+v-w|\le|u|+|v|+|w|\) and convexity of the fourth power applied to the average of these three nonnegative numbers. The second displayed inequality uses the accepted pointwise domination of the midpoint law and the nonnegativity of the fourth power. This proves the fourth-moment assertion. It holds for any center \(c\); none of the conditional class means or the endpoint mean has been substituted for the original mean.

Next let \(\tau=\operatorname{TV}(p^{\mathrm{end}},p)\). Summation class by class gives \(2q\tau=\sum_b\pi_b|\pi_b-q|\). Since \(\sum_b\pi_b=1\) and there are \(2^n\) parity classes,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_b(\pi_b-q)^2&=q-2q+2^nq^2=q(2^nq-1),\\
2q\tau
&\le\left(\sum_b\pi_b^2\right)^{1/2}
       \left(\sum_b(\pi_b-q)^2\right)^{1/2}
 =q\sqrt{2^nq-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore \(\tau\le\tfrac12\sqrt{2^nq-1}\le\tfrac12\sqrt{e^G-1}\). This calculation alone does not compare unbounded quadratic moments; the previously proved fourth-moment estimate supplies the missing input.

Fix \(a\), write \(Z(z)=a\cdot(z-m)\), and set \(\sigma_a^2=\operatorname{Var}_p(a\cdot X)\). The regularity assumption and the fourth-moment comparison with \(c=m\) give

\(\mathbb E_p Z^4\le\kappa\sigma_a^4\) and \(\mathbb E_{p^{\mathrm{end}}}Z^4\le81e^G\kappa\sigma_a^4\).

Let \(d_z^+=(p^{\mathrm{end}}_z-p_z)_+\) and \(d_z^-=(p_z-p^{\mathrm{end}}_z)_+\). Both nonnegative tables have mass \(\tau\), with \(d^+\le p^{\mathrm{end}}\) and \(d^-\le p\). Cauchy-Schwarz yields

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_zd_z^+Z(z)^2
&\le\sqrt{\tau\sum_zd_z^+Z(z)^4}
 \le9e^{G/2}\sqrt{\kappa\tau}\,\sigma_a^2,\\
\sum_zd_z^-Z(z)^2
&\le\sqrt{\tau\sum_zd_z^-Z(z)^4}
 \le\sqrt{\kappa\tau}\,\sigma_a^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

The quadratic-moment difference is the difference of these two nonnegative sums, so its absolute value is bounded by their maximum. Since \(G\ge0\), this maximum is at most \(9e^{G/2}\sqrt{\kappa\tau}\,\sigma_a^2\). Inserting the bound on \(\tau\) proves the asserted \(\varepsilon_\kappa(G)\) estimate. Finite support makes all the displayed moments finite.

If \(\sigma_a^2=0\), then \(Z(z)=0\) at every positive site of \(p\), and hence also almost surely under the endpoint marginal. Both quadratic moments vanish. The proof never divides by \(\sigma_a\), so it includes all singular directions. If \(G=0\), the parity calculation gives \(\tau=0\), equivalently \(p^{\mathrm{end}}=p\), and the conclusion holds with \(\varepsilon_\kappa(0)=0\). This also follows from the uniform parity masses in ab57fac07c0d3160, part (ii). Translations of the lattice table merely relabel parity classes and translate \(m\); the centered expressions and \(G\) are unchanged. More generally the triple identity works for every fixed affine shift \(c\), as explicitly proved above.

The triple construction does not depend on how many sites a parity class contains or on a lower bound for their individual probabilities. Even a class containing many light atoms is sampled with its correct weight \(\pi_b^2/q\), and the three midpoint marginals remain exactly the accepted \(p^{\mathrm{mid}}\). Thus the upper fourth-moment estimate prices its endpoint contribution without claiming a pointwise bound on \(p^{\mathrm{end}}/p\).

Finally, the truncated Cauchy family in ab57fac07c0d3160, part (vi), is not a counterexample: that accepted fact proves both failure of admissibility and \(G=\log2\), rather than \(G\to0\). It also fails the uniform fourth-moment premise. To check this last point directly, for its weights \(w_k^{(s)}=\mathbf1_{\{|k|\le s^2\}}/(s^2+k^2)\), symmetry gives mean zero. For every integer \(s\ge3\),

\[
\sum_k w_k^{(s)}\ge\frac1s,\qquad
\sum_k k^2w_k^{(s)}\le3s^2,\qquad
\sum_k k^4w_k^{(s)}\ge\frac{s^6}{8}.
\]

For the first bound retain \(|k|\le s\), where each weight is at least \(1/(2s^2)\). For the second bound every summand is at most one and there are \(2s^2+1\le3s^2\) sites. For the third bound retain \(\lceil s^2/2\rceil\le|k|\le s^2\). There are at least \(s^2\) such sites, and each satisfies \(k^2\ge s^2\) and \(k^2\ge s^4/4\), so \(k^4/(s^2+k^2)\ge k^2/2\ge s^4/8\). Normalizing therefore gives

\[
\frac{\mathbb E_{p^{(s)}}X^4}{(\mathbb E_{p^{(s)}}X^2)^2}
=\frac{(\sum_k w_k^{(s)})(\sum_k k^4w_k^{(s)})}
        {(\sum_k k^2w_k^{(s)})^2}
\ge\frac{s}{72}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

This calibration is consistent with the endpoint comparison and supplies no admissible refutation.
statement:
Let \(n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\), and let \(w=(w_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}\) be a nonzero, nonnegative, finitely supported admissible table: there is a finite-valued function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty)\) with \(f(z)=w_z\) at every lattice point, including every zero, such that \(f((1-t)x+ty)\ge f(x)^{1-t}f(y)^t\) for every \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(0<t<1\). Set \(W=\sum_z w_z\), \(p_z=w_z/W\), \(H_j=\sum_{v\in\mathbb Z^n}\sqrt{w_{j+v}w_{j-v}}\), \(H_*=\max_jH_j\), and \(G=\log(2^nH_*/W)\). These are the objects and normalizations of accepted fact ab57fac07c0d3160.

For \(b\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n\), set \(\pi_b=\sum_{z\equiv b\pmod2}p_z\) and \(q=\sum_b\pi_b^2\). Let \(\Gamma\) be the law of independent \(p\)-distributed \(X,Y\), conditioned on \(X\equiv Y\pmod2\), and let \(J=(X+Y)/2\) and \(p^{\mathrm{mid}}=\operatorname{law}_\Gamma(J)\). Define the endpoint marginal by \(p^{\mathrm{end}}_z=p_z\pi_{z\bmod2}/q\).

Write \(m=\sum_zp_zz\) for the mean requested in this subgoal. This vector is not the slicing dimension called \(m\) in part (iv) of ab57fac07c0d3160; that slicing parameter is not used here. Fix \(\kappa\ge0\), and suppose that for every \(a\in\mathbb R^n\),

\[
\mathbb E_p\bigl[(a\cdot(X-m))^4\bigr]
\le \kappa\bigl(\operatorname{Var}_p(a\cdot X)\bigr)^2.
\]

Then for every \(a\in\mathbb R^n\),

\[
\left|\mathbb E_\Gamma\bigl[(a\cdot(X-m))^2\bigr]
       -\operatorname{Var}_p(a\cdot X)\right|
\le \varepsilon_\kappa(G)\operatorname{Var}_p(a\cdot X),
\qquad
\varepsilon_\kappa(G)=\frac{9}{\sqrt2}\sqrt\kappa\,e^{G/2}(e^G-1)^{1/4}.
\]

In particular, \(\varepsilon_\kappa(G)\to0\) as \(G\downarrow0\), independently of dimension and of the table. The comparison is centered at the original mean \(m\), not at an assumed endpoint mean. Its upper-tail input is the following fourth-moment comparison, valid without the regularity assumption: for every \(a,c\in\mathbb R^n\),

\[
\mathbb E_\Gamma\bigl[(a\cdot(X-c))^4\bigr]
\le81\,\mathbb E_\Gamma\bigl[(a\cdot(J-c))^4\bigr]
\le81e^G\mathbb E_p\bigl[(a\cdot(X-c))^4\bigr].
\]
